reviews.title: Feels like a scam
reviews.text:
TLDR Cash grab preying on the lonely.

I’ve been on dating apps for a while now and have a pretty decent feel for the pulse of our current dating trends. Upon opening the app, I was immediately given a notification that I had 3 likes on my profile prompting me to pay money to see who it is. Subscribing to the premium lets you see the likes, subscribing to Supreme lets you date in your area. Hiding matchmaking, and more specifically local matchmaking behind a paywall is counterintuitive. Not to mention the likes I received are most likely bot accounts set up to like your profile to bait you into subscribing. I also got a text message days later saying I have new likes, this was not true. Navigating the profiles seems messy at best. Find a better app with less paywalls.

reviews.title: Concerns About the Authenticity of Profiles on This App
reviews.text:
I don't typically leave reviews like this, but after browsing hundreds of men's profiles across different states and countries, I've noticed some patterns that genuinely concern me.

Many profiles have bios and descriptions of what they're looking for that are identical word for word, sometimes following the exact same sentence structure and sequence. We're not talking about similar interests or common phrases, but entire sections that are virtually indistinguishable. It's difficult to believe that so many different people from completely different locations and backgrounds would independently write the exact same descriptions. Whether these profiles are bots, copied profiles, or AI-generated content, the repetition raises serious questions about the authenticity of the user base.

It also raises concerns about whether the likes users receive are genuine. When an app encourages people to pay to see who has liked them, users should be able to trust that those likes come from real people with genuine intentions. While I cannot confirm that fake profiles are being used to encourage subscriptions, the patterns I've observed make me question whether this possibility is being adequately addressed.

I would like to see greater transparency about profile authenticity, stronger safeguards against duplicate or fake accounts, and a dating experience that prioritizes genuine connections over simply generating likes and matches.

People are investing their time, trust, and sometimes money

reviews.title: Horrible
reviews.text:
Here’s a candid review you could post:

I gave Duet a fair chance, but ultimately deactivated my account because the app is frustrating to use and poorly designed.

First, the “likes” system doesn’t seem to work properly. I have over 9,999 likes, but no matter how many profiles I review, like, or dislike, the number never meaningfully decreases. Profiles I have already disliked often reappear multiple times. Even worse, if I dislike someone in the regular search section, they may still appear later in the “people who liked you” section, forcing me to reject the same person again.

The handling of new likes is also confusing. If I click on a new like, decide whether I’m interested, and then go back, the list of new likes disappears, making it difficult to review them efficiently.

The messaging experience is equally disappointing. I matched with dozens of people, yet almost nobody made any effort to have an actual conversation. Most messages were limited to “Hi,” “Hello,” or “How are you?” with no attempt to engage based on my profile, which is fully completed and contains plenty of information to start a meaningful conversation.

On top of that, unread messages are difficult to identify because the visual distinction is so subtle. Important messages can easily get lost among older conversations.

Overall, the app generated plenty of likes but very little meaningful interaction. Combined with the confusing interface and repetitive profiles, it felt more like an endless sorting

reviews.title: Stay away!
reviews.text:
First of all I work in digital media and I highly suspect that many of the supposed top reviews for this app are fake.
I have personally paid my money for a membership on here and it was money that was definitely wasted.
Their big selling point that you can see who is close by only comes with the top-tier subscription which is unbelievably expensive. At only half price I paid $60, I would've been completely livid had I paid $120 for the pitiful service I received.
No matter what distance you give them as a limit they will show you people within 1000 miles or more of your location--not exactly dating distance. If you don't pay for the highest level upgrade you cannot use the "nearby" function. And there's not that much activity on the app. Definitely nowhere near enough activity to even come close to justifying what they are charging.
Take a match and light your money on fire and you will get more benefit from that than paying for this app.

reviews.title: Predatory time waster

Lastly this app will constantly give you “time sensitive” notifications for absolutely no reason other than to get you to open their app. Most people turn off notifications for this app because of it but I like to actually know when someone has sent me a message so I didn’t. 

Everything negative about this app has turned me off so hard from using it I do not care if they ever fix these things. So I’m deleting it perm

reviews.title: Stay away
reviews.text:
This app is way worse at tempting you to spend money than Tinder and Bumble. For example, you have to pay to specifically see members who are nearby your location. If you pay, you will see the profiles, but you can’t swipe right or left; you are forced to either send them a crush, which is different from a like, or a praise, which is a message. BOTH crush and praise are limited to like 3 each, and then you have to pay for more. Again, you CANNOT sen these nearby members a like, even if you paid for unlimited likes, which I did.

Further, the filters are limited, and you are FORCED to see people outside of your preferences such as age range and distance from you. Other apps like Tinder give you the option to not see people outside of your preferences. Duet does NOT, so you will see people who live in different states not even 50 miles close to you.

Further, even though Duet advertises no fake profiles, I’m convinced that it will choose random accounts and force those accounts to send you a like. For example, the moment my account was created, I received four likes instantly, but obviously couldn’t see who liked me until I bought the subscription. Three of them were not even in the same state as me, and the only one I liked back hasn’t even replied to my message. In fact before I liked them, I saw that they lived in the same county as me, and after I matched, their location changed to a different state.

reviews.title: This app is the less reliable Walmart version of Tinder
reviews.text: DO NOT DOWNLOAD NOR PAY FOR THIS APP! This app advertised itself constantly on social media platforms (mainly on Tik Tok) as a sort of want-to-be Tinder. While in some regards it is a Tinder knock-off (pay-to-use, etc.,) it is worse as constant bug and glitches prevent even the most basic functionality. If/ when you pay to upgrade your subscription you are taken from the app and sent to an external browser window to then pay. However, despite payment confirmation on the external browser (not to mention proof payment from the funds withdrawn from your bank account), the app frequently seems to forget about the upgraded user status and will revert a paid user back to the same status and usability as if they were an unpaid user. Another major flaw with the app is that despite having a user's location, and despite supposedly changeable location preferences that a user can alter, this function doesn't work. A user will not be shown other user profiles according to and determined by their own location and selected location preferences, but instead be shown profiles that are hundreds of miles away, and subsequently (and realistically) nullifying any potential matches and any development of a connection between users. Overall I'd say Duet is a fraudulent app that uses constant deceptive and misleading advertisements centered on the chance of rapid matches and sex appeal to cover up the developer's lack of skill, greed, and unoriginality.

reviews.title: Matching System Broken
reviews.text:
It seems to only show you other “popular” profiles that are extremely far away, and only when it notices you’ve swiped “no” a bunch of times on men local to you. The few men I did match with somewhat near me either 1. Never messaged me back, even if I messaged them first or
2. Were insanely boring and had ZERO conversational skills and or were seeking to “hook up.”

 I’m assuming if I paid some type of subscription fee I would all the sudden start seeing the “popular profiles” near me. 

Also…
🚨🚨🚨It’s incredibly disheartening I would have to pay $$$ to see people who like me. It takes away the opportunity that I could ever find someone. Making me waste more time swiping on people who aren’t even interested in me and thus wasting more time is ridiculous. For that, I think this app is more focused on making money rather than match making. 

The only thing I do have to say, is the layout and set up of the app layout is nice and it’s easy to understand. The quizzes it uses to help create matches for you are quick and simple. If you want a free dating app with a simple easy to use interface this is a great app. I guess I would just be prepared that you may need to invest some time in order to find someone in this app. Simply because the distance and age ratio show people super far away and a couple years outside your dating preference. Thus you have to spend extra time swiping on the obvious “no’s”.

reviews.title: Another app where guys are set up to fail
reviews.text: Gentleman, this app is bad. It’s another “pay and THEN we will show you who you like” app, otherwise you’ll never see who liked you. The additional features you get for paying is a waste of time. They don’t have the preference option working at all, like they keep suggestion women from 200 miles away, even though I have the distance set to 30 miles. And funny enough there are only 3 preference options; age, distance, and sex. So far the sex one is the only one that works, but that’s it for preference options?? You can’t set up a preference if you’re ok with meeting people with kids. The “blind date” feature is a dud too, they set me up with one woman who didn’t respond back, so I unmatched to try again, and it’s been 48 hours and it hasn’t matched me with anyone. The straw that broke the camels back was the turbo feature, where supposedly you get 10x the views. Well funny enough the app has a record of who looks at your profile and when I used the turbo feature, NOT ONE VIEW ON MY PROFILE. I guess 10 x 0 =0, but come on Duet that’s it??? You see and look at all these reviews and I’m suspicious of the authenticity of them. Anyways in conclusion, it’s bad and it doesn’t help guys in the slightest. You are better off sticking to the other ones.
